title: When you land
body:
Tottori has its own small regional airport (Tottori Sand Dunes Conan Airport, code TTJ) with ANA service to/from Haneda, but the more robust routing for a party of eight is Shinkansen to Okayama or Shin-Osaka, then a limited express (Super Inaba or Super Hakuto/Super Oki/Super Matsukaze) onward to Tottori Station — it isn't dependent on one small airport's schedule.

⚠ This guide doesn't yet have a confirmed departure airport or flight on file, so no specific routing is booked in as fact — the Booking checklist below flags it.

title: Local essentials
body:
Rural Tottori runs on cash more than Tokyo or Osaka does — Misasa Onsen and Kurayoshi's old town both have plenty of card-shy small shops and ryokan. ⚠ 7-Eleven (Seven Bank) ATMs are the commonly cited way to withdraw on a foreign card, and Japan Post ATMs back them up in smaller towns on bank hours — but that guidance is flagged rather than confirmed in this guide (see the Money tab), so check your own card network before you rely on it. ⚠ Convenience-store density drops noticeably once you're off the San'in line — stock up on cash in Tottori or Kurayoshi before settling into Misasa Onsen for the night.

The reference exchange rate and the cash-vs-card picture live on the Money tab.

title: Entry & documents
body: See the Entry requirements card for the assumed passport (US, visa-free up to 90 days). If anyone in the party carries a different passport, flag it before departure — this guide has only researched the US case.

title: Phone & data
body: An eSIM (Ubigi, Airalo, and similar Japan-wide plans) or an airport pocket-wifi rental both cover this itinerary fine — San'in region coverage is standard 4G/5G along the rail line and in the towns this trip visits, including Misasa Onsen.

title: Booking checklist
body: Two items on this trip are genuinely time-sensitive, not boilerplate: the Yakiniku Masashige dinner for eight needs a phone call, not the web form, and the Nageiredo climb is a same-day weather call with no way to pre-book around it.
checklist: Flights — no departure airport confirmed yet; pin this down early since it also decides whether Tottori Airport (ANA/Haneda) or a Shinkansen + limited express routing makes more sense

Accommodation — a Misasa Onsen ryokan with rooms for 8 (likely split across 2–4 rooms); confirm step-free or ground-floor room availability given 2 travelers with low walking tolerance, and ask whether the ryokan runs a free reserved shuttle from Kurayoshi Station as an alternative to the public bus
Dinner at Yakiniku Masashige, Kurayoshi — call 0858-26-2919 to book a table for 8; the online form's party-size selector doesn't reach 8 (confirmed on the booking page)

Nageiredo climb — no advance booking exists; treat it as a same-day go/no-go depending on weather, and have the free Yohaijo viewing platform as the fallback plan for anyone in the group who shouldn't attempt the climb
Kurayoshi→Misasa fallback — for a guaranteed single-vehicle transfer instead of the public bus, reserve a 9-seat Hinomaru Hire jumbo taxi ahead of time (0858-22-3155)
